aiOverview.content: The Artemis II crew will spend approximately 10 days in space for their lunar mission. This mission, launching in April 2026, involves navigating around the Moon before splashing down in the Pacific Ocean. The mission tests systems for future deep-space missions and sets a record for distance from Earth. Artemis II Mission Details: Duration: 10 days. Objective: Test Orion spacecraft systems, including manual steering and radiation protection, while orbiting the Moon. Milestone: The crew will travel further into space than any human has before. Other Spaceflight Durations: International Space Station (ISS): Typical missions for astronauts on the ISS last about six months. Long-Duration Records: Some astronauts, such as Frank Rubio, have spent over a year (371 days) in space.
